HomeStyle Retail, Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeStyle Retail, Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeStyle Retail's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Rivera, Chief Merchandising Officer; and Emma Patel, Chief Stores Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeStyle Retail's performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover six key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: Our four-pillar framework—Store Network Optimization, Omnichannel Acceleration, Supply Chain Resilience, and Customer-Centric Innovation—is delivering strong progress. This underpinned our Q3 comparable store sales growth of 5.8%, well ahead of the retail sector average, and lifted adjusted EBITDA margins to levels like 12.1%, up over 100 basis points year-over-year. Starting with Store Network Optimization, we're prioritizing high-return investments across our roughly 1,300-store footprint in home goods and improvement. We opened 25 new stores this quarter in high-growth Sunbelt areas such as Texas and Florida, where population growth tops 2% annually based on U.S. Census figures. These 120,000-square-foot greenfield sites are on track to hit EBITDA breakeven in 18 months, matching our 85% historical success rate. We also remodeled 150 stores with the NextGen format, featuring open layouts similar to recent Home Depot updates, expanded pro-contractor areas, and EV charging to tap into the trades segment now at 28% of sales. On the flip side, we closed 15 low-performing stores in low-density Northeast areas like upstate New York and rural Pennsylvania, where traffic had dropped 12% over three years from e-commerce shifts and demographic changes. Those closures freed up $45 million, redirected to remodels. As a result, sales per square foot climbed 7% to $650, and inventory turns rose to 5.2x from 4.8x. For FY2025, expect 75 net new stores, 60% in Sunbelt and Midwest spots like Indianapolis, adding short-term capex drag but 400 basis points to long-term ROIC.

Moving to Omnichannel Acceleration, our brick-and-mortar stores are evolving into seamless ecosystems. Omnichannel sales hit 32% of revenue, surpassing peers like Lowe's. Buy Online, Pick Up In-Store orders jumped 45% year-over-year to 25% of digital volume, with 95% fulfilled in two hours via micro-fulfillment in 400 stores. We've added Symbotic robots to cut pick errors 60% and lift BOPIS 30%, echoing Best Buy's model. Same-day delivery through DoorDash and Instacart covers 85% of ZIP codes, dropping costs 18% to $4.50 per order with AI routing. In pilots in Atlanta and Phoenix, basket sizes for under-35s rose 15%. Mobile app downloads topped 2.5 million, boosted by AR tools for appliances, tripling conversions. We're committing $250 million next year for 40% penetration and 20% lower acquisition costs using data from our 45-million-member rewards program.

On Supply Chain Resilience, we've hit 92% in-stock on core items, up from 84%, via dual-sourcing with partners like Procter & Gamble. Inventory is lean at 12 weeks, aiding 90 basis point gross margin gains to 34.2%. Our new 1.2-million-square-foot Dallas DC serves 350 stores with blockchain traceability, trimming import lead times 25%. West Coast comps shone at 6.1% with housing starts up 8% per NAHB, while Midwest was softer at 1.9% from auto issues, offset by vendor rebates for 3-5% pricing stability on 70% of goods. Sustainability efforts include 40% low-emission ocean freight via Maersk, boosting private-label appeal among millennials by 15%.

Finally, Customer-Centric Innovation: Rewards membership grew 18% to 48 million, with paid tiers adding $120 million in fees, up 25%. Redemption hit 62% via Salesforce AI segmenting 12 personas from pros to newbies. Private-label BuildPro now has 2,500 SKUs at 45% margins versus 32% national, holding 22% in tools. Edge kiosks in 500 stores enable price matching and AR consults, upping conversions 22%. We've upskilled 15,000 associates, cutting turnover to 28% from 42%. These pillars synergize—omnichannel doubles store traffic, with 68% BOPIS add-ons. Amid flat 1.2% consumer spending growth per BEA, value bundles like our Fix-A-Leak service build resilience. Risks like tariffs on 15% Chinese imports are hedged 70%. We see 300 basis points EBITDA lift in FY2025, 3-5% comps, $1.2 billion free cash flow, capex at 4.5% of sales in our $1.1 trillion market growing 4% CAGR per FMI.

2. E-Commerce Growth: One standout was e-commerce sales, up a strong 28% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, now 22% of total net sales from 17% last year—our 11th consecutive double-digit quarter amid retail headwinds like inflation and weak confidence. Gross Merchandise Value reached $1.35 billion, +30% YoY, from higher traffic, better conversions, and 12% AOV growth to $145 via upselling bundles like Threshold kitchenware with appliances, plus promotions on bedding and outdoor living up 45% online. Monthly unique visitors soared 35% to 45 million, mobile at 68% of sessions from 62%. Our Q1-relauched app with AR try-before-buy for furniture drove 52% download growth and 4.8% in-app conversions, matching Wayfair, powered by Google Cloud ML for 22% higher add-to-cart. U.S. sales, 92% of digital, grew 31%, Northeast up 42% with DoorDash same-day at 15% penetration. BOPIS surged 48% to 2.5 million units, 40% adding in-store buys. U.K. and Canada platforms rose 18% with local micro-fulfillment; Europe site-to-store next quarter vs. Amazon/Next. Our $250 million YTD CapEx in 15 store-co-located automated centers cut delivery to under 2 days for 85% U.S. orders, costs 15% lower—outpacing Amazon's 9% growth. CAC steady at $28, down 5% via loyalty's 18 million actives lifting repeats to 65%. Q4 e-com eyes 25-30% growth with holidays, $400 million Black Friday digital, AI pricing; full-year 20%+ penetration, positive FCF from efficiencies. We're reimagining retail as one ecosystem.

3. Store Performance: Comparable store sales—or comps—rose 5.8% year-over-year, our sixth straight positive quarter and accelerating 210 basis points from Q2's 3.7%, beating retail's 2.9% per Johnson Redbook and driving 60% of top-line. Traffic increased 2.1%, from Home Refresh Days promotions and 250 remodels (15% of base) lifting comps 12.4% with omnichannel zones, AI self-scan kiosks, interactive demos—conversions up 80 bps to 28.5%. Average unit retail gained 3.6% on mix to big-ticket hardlines (+7.2%, appliances/outdoor from housing demand) and softlines (+4.1% bedding/decor); apparel -0.5% but improving as StyleForge private label wins Gen Z via TikTok. Southeast (400+ stores) led +8.1% on migration, Nashville micro-DC BOPIS +28%; Midwest +4.3% on essentials; West Coast -1.2% from wildfires/tourism, ex-West +7.4%. MyHome Rewards (18 million actives) drove 16% of comp sales from personalized offers, turns 5.2x, shrink 1.4% via RFID in 100 stores, PLCC 22%. Despite 3.2% CPI, supply tailwinds like 40% freight drops aid high-velocity SKUs. Q4 comps guided 4-6%, +150 bps from 100 more remodels, curbside returns. Our showrooms excel on big-ticket vs. Amazon/peers.

4. Marketing Initiatives: Marketing and ad expenses hit $45.2 million in Q3, +15.8% YoY from $39 million, TTM $178.4 million +12.2%, 2.8% of sales up 30 bps; YTD $89.7 million at 2.7%, guiding full-year 2.6-2.8%. This ROI-focused ramp counters spending moderation and ad inflation. Digital took 62% ($28.1 million, + from 48%), programmatic video/CTV 35% up 28% via Trade Desk DSP geofencing with 45 million Rewards data. ROAS 4.8x from 4.2x on Vertex AI DCO for Meta/Google, private-label kitchen lift 22%, CAC $22.50 down 8%, retention 72%; SEM $9.8 million +20% on spiking searches. Traditional 28% ($12.6 million +6%), TV/radio 3.5x ROAS despite CPM +11%, shifted to OOH billboards +18% visits per Placer.ai. Print/mail 10% down 12% to $4.5 million, digitized to app for 25% CAC cut, 65% redemptions. In-store $4.5 million +25%, AI signage in 450 stores +14% impulse, Home Refresh Workshops with Sherwin-Williams 2.5x ROAS via TikTok 10M views. Sunbelt +22% expenses for 9% comps, 5.2x ROAS; Northeast +10% on OOH/loyalty. Canada CAD 8.2M +18% on Meta/NHL +12% traffic; Mexico pilots 4.1x. Total ROAS 4.6x beats RetailX 3.9x. Q3 $48-50M 2.7-2.9%, holiday CTV +25%, CMS for BOPIS; FY 5%+ ROAS via clean rooms. Brick-and-mortar experiential plus digital amplification.

5. Supply Chain Optimization: Supply chain efficiencies drove 12% gross margin expansion this quarter, or 250 bps contribution. Costs fell 17% to 6.8% of sales from 8.2%, turns +22% to 5.5x beating NRF 4.8x, DOIH 58 days aiding seasonal clears without markdowns. In-stock 97.2% + from 91%, on-time 98.5% + from 89%, freight/unit -14%. Savings $185 million QoQ, $750M run-rate or 150 bps op margin vs. 4% wage inflation. $450M over 18 months transformed: Blue Yonder AI demand sensing on SAP cut forecast error 28% incorporating POS/weather/CPI, 92% accuracy 52 weeks out. AutoStore goods-to-person in 12/28 DCs +40% picks to 450/hour; DFW mega-DC AMRs -25% labor. RFID 85% inbound -15 bps shrink to 1.1%. VMI with 150 suppliers like PepsiCo freed $120M capital. Micro-fulfillment pilots in Chicago/LA for <2hr BOPIS. North America sourcing China down to 28% from 45%, nearshoring Mexico/Vietnam +35% volumes cut leads 45-22 days. Europe Dublin hub -18% transit, €22M duties save. Sustainability: logistics emissions -11% electric/rail, 62% loyalty eco-prefer. Vs. Amazon, our 5,000+ stores are micro-DCs. FY25 $300M for 50 MFCs, blockchain perishables, 10-12% more cuts. Raised FY24 margins 42.5%, FCF $2.2B. Our moat.

6. Loyalty Program Update: Drilling into traffic versus ticket for our 4.2% comps this quarter—strongest in six quarters, topping NRG/Placer.ai flat index amid 3.1% CPI, 1.8% income growth. Formula: +1.8% traffic, +0.9% conversion, +1.5% ticket. Traffic third straight positive vs. -2.1% prior, +3% share; Sunbelt +4.2% migration/Phoenix ramps; Northeast/Midwest flat/-0.5% office/weather; West/SE exurbs +2.1% express/BOPIS; weekdays +1.2%, weekends +3.5% Warrior promos like TJX. Ticket to $52.40 +1.5%: UPT 2.41 +1.2%, AUR $21.75 +0.3%. Apparel +2.8% Levi's/Lululemon; home +1.1% bundles; hardlines flat private-label 28% +300 bps. Vs. Target +1.3%, Kohl's +1.8%. Funnel: traffic x conv = +2.7% trans, x ticket =4.2%; kiosks 40% stores +8% add-ons. BOPIS/ship-from 18% digital +25% traffic; app 14M users +22% ML geo-pushes +120 bps conv; $150M CapEx fixtures/scents +15% dwell/0.3 UPT; dynamic pricing 38.2% margins. Q3 traffic +2.5-3%, ticket trade-up/private vs. tariffs (12% big-ticket). Sunbelt 25 news +40 bps lift, TJX-like value/experiential.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Total revenue reached $5.5 billion, up 7% year-over-year, propelled by 5.8% comps and e-commerce acceleration to 22% mix. Gross margin expanded to 38.5%, driven by supply chain gains like 15% lower fulfillment and freight, favorable private-label shift to 28% sales at higher margins, and optimized inventory turns at 5.5x. Operating expenses came in at $1.82 billion, or 33.1% of revenue, reflecting disciplined scaling with marketing up 16% but ROAS at 4.6x, offset by labor efficiencies from upskilling. Net income was $480 million, delivering $1.35 per share. Cash flow from operations generated $700 million, supporting $250 million CapEx in omnichannel and stores. Inventory levels are currently healthy at 12 weeks of supply, down 15% YoY with 97% in-stock.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Rivera, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, and after that to Emma Patel to discuss store operations.

David Rivera, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we launched our expanded BuildPro private-label line, now spanning 2,500 SKUs in tools, fasteners, and essentials, which has captured 22% category share and delivered outsized 45% gross margins compared to national brands. Early traction has been exceptional, contributing to hardlines comps over 7% and validating our innovation push—we're excited about upcoming launches in sustainable home refresh categories.

Emma Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented NextGen remodels across 150 locations, incorporating open-concept layouts, pro desks, EV charging, and AI kiosks, and are seeing positive results with average 12.4% comp lifts, higher dwell times, and conversion gains.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, John. Inflation remains a headwind with CPI at 3.2%, stretching consumer wallets on discretionary, but our value engineering like private-label expansion to 28%, bundling, and loyalty personalization drove resilient 5.8% comps—outpacing sector averages. Loyalty members redeem 62-65% on targeted offers, and efficiencies offset promo intensity, positioning us well versus peers facing softer home goods.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, Emily. We're guiding Q4 comps to 4% to 6%, incorporating 150 basis points from additional remodels, nationwide curbside enhancements, and holiday omnichannel ramps. This assumes stable gas prices and no major disruptions, with traffic +2.5-3% and ticket leverage from mix shift and private labels.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Robert. Our transformation delivered 17% cost cuts to 6.8% of sales, 5.5x turns, 97% in-stock via AI forecasting down 28% error, AutoStore automation +40% picks, RFID shrink reduction, and nearshoring trimming leads 22 days. $185 million quarterly savings, scaling to $750 million run-rate—key to 250 bps margin help and competing with Amazon's speed through our store network.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Anna Kim (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great to hear, Anna. Our rewards program, at 45-48 million members including paid tiers generating $120 million fees up 25%, drove 16% of comp sales, 62% redemption via AI personas, and 65% repeat rates. It lowers CAC 5-8%, boosts BOPIS add-ons 40-68%, and fuels omnichannel traffic—core to our customer-centric pillar.

Operator:
Thank you. As a follow-up, our next question from Laura Chen with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen (Deutsche Bank):
How are marketing efficiencies supporting holiday plans?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Laura. With ROAS at 4.6x and digital 62% mix yielding 4.8x, we're ramping Q4 to $48-50 million or 2.7-2.9% of sales, emphasizing CTV +25%, geofenced BOPIS promos, and app pushes for 20% traffic lift—building on Sunbelt successes and targeting 5%+ full-year ROAS expansion.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
